sentences.latin: Sollemne est mihi, domine, omnia de quibus dubito ad te referre.
sentences.english: It is my custom, lord, to refer to you all matters about which I am in doubt.

sentences.latin: Quis enim potest melius vel cunctationem meam regere vel ignorantiam instruere?
sentences.english: For who can better either guide my hesitation or instruct my ignorance?

sentences.latin: Cognitionibus de Christianis interfui numquam: ideo nescio quid et quatenus aut puniri soleat aut quaeri.
sentences.english: I have never been present at trials of Christians: therefore I do not know what is usually punished or investigated, or to what extent.

sentences.latin: Nec mediocriter haesitavi, sitne aliquod discrimen aetatum, an quamlibet teneri nihil a robustioribus differant; detur paenitentiae venia, an ei, qui omnino Christianus fuit, desisse non prosit; nomen ipsum, si flagitiis careat, an flagitia cohaerentia nomini puniantur.
sentences.english: Nor have I hesitated only a little: whether there is any distinction of ages, or whether however young they are they differ in no way from the stronger; whether pardon is to be granted to repentance, or whether for one who has been a Christian at all it does no good to have ceased; whether the name itself, even if it lacks crimes, or only the crimes attached to the name, should be punished.

sentences.latin: Interim, in iis qui ad me tamquam Christiani deferebantur, hunc sum secutus modum.
sentences.english: Meanwhile, with those who were brought before me as Christians, I have followed this method.

sentences.latin: Interrogavi ipsos an essent Christiani.
sentences.english: I asked them whether they were Christians.

sentences.latin: Confitentes iterum ac tertio interrogavi supplicium minatus: perseverantes duci iussi.
sentences.english: Those who confessed I asked a second and a third time, threatening punishment: those who persisted I ordered to be led away to execution.

sentences.latin: Neque enim dubitabam, qualecumque esset quod faterentur, pertinaciam certe et inflexibilem obstinationem debere puniri.
sentences.english: For I did not doubt that, whatever it was that they were confessing, their stubbornness certainly and inflexible obstinacy ought to be punished.

sentences.latin: Fuerunt alii similis amentiae, quos, quia cives Romani erant, adnotavi in urbem remittendos.
sentences.english: There were others of similar madness, whom, because they were Roman citizens, I noted as needing to be sent back to the City.

sentences.latin: Mox ipso tractatu, ut fieri solet, diffundente se crimine plures species inciderunt.
sentences.english: Soon, in the very course of the proceedings, as is usually the case, the charge spreading itself, more variations arose.

sentences.latin: Propositus est libellus sine auctore multorum nomina continens.
sentences.english: An anonymous document was put forward containing the names of many people.

sentences.latin: Qui negabant esse se Christianos aut fuisse, cum praeeunte me deos appellarent et imagini tuae, quam propter hoc iusseram cum simulacris numinum afferri, ture ac vino supplicarent, praeterea male dicerent Christo, quorum nihil cogi posse dicuntur qui sunt re vera Christiani, dimittendos putavi.
sentences.english: Those who denied that they were or had been Christians, when, with me leading them, they invoked the gods and made supplication with incense and wine to your image, which I had ordered to be brought in for this purpose along with the statues of the gods, and besides cursed Christ — none of which, it is said, those who are truly Christians can be compelled to do — I thought should be released.

sentences.latin: Alii ab indice nominati esse se Christianos dixerunt et mox negaverunt; fuisse quidem, sed desisse, quidam ante triennium, quidam ante plures annos, non nemo etiam ante viginti.
sentences.english: Others named by an informer said that they were Christians and then denied it; they had been, indeed, but had ceased, some three years before, some many years before, a few even twenty years before.

sentences.latin: Hi quoque omnes et imaginem tuam deorumque simulacra venerati sunt et Christo male dixerunt.
sentences.english: These too all venerated both your image and the statues of the gods and cursed Christ.

sentences.latin: Affirmabant autem hanc fuisse summam vel culpae suae vel erroris, quod essent soliti stato die ante lucem convenire, carmenque Christo quasi deo dicere secum invicem, seque sacramento non in scelus aliquod obstringere, sed ne furta ne latrocinia ne adulteria committerent, ne fidem fallerent, ne depositum appellati abnegarent.
sentences.english: They asserted, however, that this had been the sum of their fault or error: that they had been accustomed to meet on a fixed day before dawn and to recite a hymn antiphonally to Christ as to a god, and to bind themselves by oath not to any crime, but that they would not commit thefts, robberies, or adulteries, that they would not break their word, that they would not deny a deposit when called upon to return it.

sentences.latin: Quibus peractis morem sibi discedendi fuisse rursusque coeundi ad capiendum cibum, promiscuum tamen et innoxium; quod ipsum facere desisse post edictum meum, quo secundum mandata tua hetaerias esse vetueram.
sentences.english: When these things had been done, it had been their custom to depart and gather again to take food, but ordinary and harmless food; and even this they had ceased to do after my edict, by which, according to your instructions, I had forbidden secret societies.

sentences.latin: Quo magis necessarium credidi ex duabus ancillis, quae ministrae dicebantur, quid esset veri, et per tormenta quaerere.
sentences.english: On account of this I believed it all the more necessary to seek the truth from two slave-women, who were called deaconesses, even by means of torture.

sentences.latin: Nihil aliud inveni quam superstitionem pravam et immodicam.
sentences.english: I found nothing other than a depraved and excessive superstition.

sentences.latin: Ideo dilata cognitione ad consulendum te decucurri.
sentences.english: Therefore, postponing the inquiry, I have hastened to consult you.

sentences.latin: Visa est enim mihi res digna consultatione, maxime propter periclitantium numerum.
sentences.english: For the matter has seemed to me worthy of consultation, especially because of the number of those at risk.

sentences.latin: Multi enim omnis aetatis, omnis ordinis, utriusque sexus etiam vocantur in periculum et vocabuntur.
sentences.english: For many of every age, of every rank, of both sexes also are being called and will be called into danger.

sentences.latin: Neque civitates tantum, sed vicos etiam atque agros superstitionis istius contagio pervagata est; quae videtur sisti et corrigi posse.
sentences.english: And not only cities, but villages too and country districts have been pervaded by the contagion of this superstition; which seems able to be checked and corrected.

sentences.latin: Certe satis constat prope iam desolata templa coepisse celebrari, et sacra sollemnia diu intermissa repeti passimque venire victimas, quarum adhuc rarissimus emptor inveniebatur.
sentences.english: Certainly it is sufficiently agreed that the temples, almost already deserted, have begun to be frequented again, and that the customary rites long interrupted are being resumed, and that everywhere sacrificial victims are being sold, of which until recently a buyer was very rarely found.

sentences.latin: Ex quo facile est opinari, quae turba hominum emendari possit, si sit paenitentiae locus.
sentences.english: From which it is easy to suppose what a crowd of people could be set right, if there were a place for repentance.
